{"id": "5542930d-038b-4bf5-9f71-68abae6313ea", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good question — this is one of those cases where "the IAM role already has the right permissions" is true but still not sufficient, because Amazon Personalize evaluates more than just the role's identity policy. Here's the chain, in the order Personalize actually checks it:

**1. Role trust policy** — the role must trust `personalize.amazonaws.com` to assume it. If this is missing, you'd typically see an `AssumeRole`-flavored error rather than this one, but worth a quick check.

**2. Role identity policy** (`s3:GetObject`, `s3:ListBucket` on the bucket/objects) — you've confirmed this is fine.

**3. S3 bucket resource policy** — this is the most common denying hop. Per AWS's own troubleshooting guidance for this exact error, Personalize requires the **bucket policy itself** to explicitly name the service role's ARN as a principal, separate from the role's own identity policy. An identity policy that grants `s3:GetObject`/`s3:ListBucket` is necessary but not sufficient — if the bucket policy doesn't also have a statement allowing that exact role ARN, Personalize gets denied at the bucket level even though the role "has" the permissions. This is especially easy to miss if the dataset group and bucket live in different accounts — in that case the bucket policy must include the role ARN explicitly, since cross-account access doesn't flow from identity policy alone.

**4. KMS key policy (if the bucket uses SSE-KMS)** — AWS's documentation calls this out specifically: for dataset import jobs, **only the KMS key's resource policy matters** — any `kms:Decrypt`/`kms:GenerateDataKey` grant on the role's own IAM policy is not even evaluated. If the bucket is encrypted with a customer-managed key (or even the default `aws/s3` key) and that key's policy doesn't grant the Personalize role `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey`, and `kms:ListGrants`, you get this same "Insufficient privileges" message — it looks identical to an S3 permissions failure.

Given you've already ruled out #2, the denying hop is almost certainly **#3 (missing/incomplete bucket policy statement for the role ARN)** or **#4 (KMS key policy)** if the bucket is encrypted.

If you want, give me the role ARN and bucket name and I can pull the actual bucket policy and KMS key policy from your account to confirm which one is the culprit.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
